questions.q: What is the primary physical setting of the luncheon in the story?
questions.a: The primary physical setting is Foyot's, an expensive restaurant in Paris frequented by French senators. A wrong answer (e.g., "the narrator's apartment" or "a café") reveals the student cannot distinguish the main setting from incidental locations mentioned in the flashback.

questions.q: Explain how the description of the restaurant's prices creates atmosphere in the opening scene.
questions.a: The high prices establish an atmosphere of anxiety and foreboding because the narrator realizes he cannot afford the meal, setting up the tension that drives the story. A wrong answer that only mentions "the prices are high" without linking to the narrator's emotional state shows a lack of understanding of atmosphere as mood created for the reader.

questions.q: If the story were set in a modest café instead of Foyot's, how would the atmosphere and irony change? Provide two specific differences.
questions.a: In a modest café, the narrator would not fear the bill, so the atmosphere of panic would disappear; the irony of the lady's "light eating" would be less sharp because the cost gap would be smaller. A wrong answer that says "the story would be the same" fails to apply the concept that setting shapes atmosphere and irony.

questions.q: Compare the atmosphere before the bill arrives with the atmosphere after the narrator pays. How does the shift reflect the story's structure?
questions.a: Before the bill, the atmosphere is tense and panic-stricken; after paying, it shifts to resignation and bitter humor as the narrator walks away penniless. This shift mirrors the narrative arc from rising tension to ironic resolution. A wrong answer that describes only one atmosphere misses the structural analysis.

questions.q: The narrator says, "I have had my revenge at last" because the lady now weighs twenty-one stone. Is the setting of the final revelation (the theater, years later) effective for this closure? Justify.
questions.a: Yes, the theater setting — where they first met — creates a circular structure that emphasizes the passage of time and the physical consequence of her gluttony, making the revenge feel fated. A wrong answer that says "no, any setting would work" fails to evaluate the symbolic function of setting.

questions.q: Write a 3-sentence paragraph describing a new setting for a similar luncheon (e.g., a five-star hotel in Mumbai) that would create an analogous atmosphere of financial dread for a struggling writer.
questions.a: A good answer will name a specific expensive Mumbai venue (e.g., The Taj Mahal Palace), mention menu prices that exceed the writer's budget, and convey the writer's internal panic. A poor answer will be vague about the setting or omit the atmosphere of dread.
